A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VGGSounder study and contain the complete main text and Appendices A–D. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the figures, tables and mathematics.

before.justification: V3 reports original annotation statistics, evaluations of eleven models, and robustness and label-source analyses, including Tables 2–5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical evaluations, revises their results, and adds outcomes from a human-reviewed annotation cleanup in Appendix D.6.

M1.justification: Appendix D.6 adds a benchmark-curation step: automated identification of potentially noisy annotations, targeted human review, and removal of clips without valid labels. The original proposal/voting pipeline, evaluated model architectures and inference procedures are otherwise retained.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same VGGSound-derived, 309-class audio-visual classification task, modalities and meta-class scenarios. Annotation corrections and sample removals revise the existing benchmark without introducing a different task, domain or population.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same four embedding models and seven foundation models. Adding AV-Siam to Table 2's finetuning caption corrects an omission: v3 already evaluated it there and described its finetuning in Section 5 and Appendix C.1.

E3.justification: The evaluation ground truth is substantially revised: Appendix D.6 reports corrections to label/modality sets for 3,616 videos and removal of 182 videos. Table 1 changes the reported size from 15.4k to 15.1k clips. Evaluation targets and membership therefore change, while metrics, top-k choices and prompting protocols remain the same; model retraining is not established.

E4.justification: V4 adds annotation-error audit outcomes in Appendix D.6. Existing top-k sensitivity, meta-class robustness and label-source ablations retain their questions but receive revised evidence in Tables 3, 7, 9–14 and 17. No new model robustness test family is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests for the benchmark results. No seed, run-count or statistical estimation procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Central benchmark scores and appendix results are extensively revised. In Table 2, audio-visual F1 changes from 42.62 to 45.97 for CAV-MAE and from 53.74 to 56.96 for Gemini 1.5 Pro. Table 3 changes Unified-IO 2's visual background-music delta F1 from +1.15 to -0.73. Dataset distributions also change, including Figure 1's 40,000+ labels becoming 38,000+. These are evaluations against revised annotations and membership, not demonstrated model performance gains under identical conditions.

T1.justification: Equation (1) and the mathematical treatment of modality confusion are unchanged. The October 2025 metric-definition revision described in Appendix D.6, with historical results in Table 18, already appears in v3.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a modality-aware multi-label benchmark, evaluation of audio-visual models, and measurement of modality confusion. Claims about modality preferences and challenging meta-class subsets are not substantively revised.

C2.justification: Sections 5–7 and Appendix D retain their interpretations of modality bias, confounder effects and human versus automatic annotations. The cleanup adds factual curation outcomes without substantively revising these explanations or adding applicability limitations.

D1.justification: V4 documents the May 2026 audit, human correction and invalid-sample removal process, including preservation of annotations on untouched samples. Table 1 also identifies the older 15.4k-sample release as v0.1.6. Model/checkpoint descriptions, evaluator prompts and access links are otherwise unchanged; detailed audit-selection rules are not supplied.

R1.justification: The same 91 references and substantive relationships to earlier benchmarks and models are retained. Related-work edits are grammatical, with reference text merely reflowing across pages.

P1.justification: V4 corrects grammar and model-name formatting, expands the acknowledgements, and appends the May 2026 changelog entry. The section organization and almost all explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing distribution and radar plots are updated within their original formats; Figure 8 changes class ordering and axis ranges. Table 1 gains a version footnote, and Table 18 moves upward on page 27 to accommodate the cleanup account. There is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The reported human correction of 3,616 videos, removal of 5,928 spurious label rows and 182 invalid samples, and correction/addition of 3,140 rows address a substantial ground-truth defect in the paper's central benchmark. This cleanup and the revised evaluations materially strengthen its usefulness. Reporting remains imperfect: Table 4 and parts of the label-ablation discussion are not reconciled with updated Tables 16–17. These shortcomings limit clarity but do not outweigh the documented repair of the benchmark.
